q: In the horizontal devolution of the divisible pool of central taxes among the States recommended by the Fifteenth Finance Commission, the weight assigned to the criterion of 'area' is:
e: The Fifteenth Finance Commission gave 15 per cent weight to area in horizontal devolution, along with income distance, population, demographic performance, forest and ecology and tax effort.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States under Article 268 of the Constitution do not form part of the Consolidated Fund of India, the proceeds being assigned to the States.
2. The taxes levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States under Article 269 of the Constitution likewise do not form part of the Consolidated Fund of India, the net proceeds being paid to the States.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct under Articles 268 and 269. Duties and taxes there are for the States, and their net proceeds do not form part of the Consolidated Fund of India.

q: Exchequer control over public expenditure is primarily concerned with:

options.A: Suggesting economies in the estimates framed by the Ministries
options.B: Examining the accounts of the Government after the expenditure has been incurred
options.C: Assessing the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of Government programmes
options.D: Regulating the drawal of moneys and the making of payments out of the Government account, so that payments are made only against duly authorised grants and appropriations and in accordance with the prescribed procedure

e: Exchequer control regulates drawal and payment of money from the Government account so that payments are made only against authorised grants and appropriations and by the prescribed procedure.

q: During the general discussion on the Union Budget in Parliament:

options.A: The Budget as a whole and the policies underlying it are discussed, but no motion is moved and no vote is taken
options.B: The Demands for Grants of the Ministries are voted one by one
options.C: Cut motions are moved and disposed of
options.D: The Appropriation Bill is introduced and passed

e: In the general discussion on the Budget, the Budget as a whole and its underlying policies are discussed. No motion is moved and no vote is taken at that stage.

q: A Money Bill in Parliament can be introduced:

options.A: By any member of the Lok Sabha
options.C: By any member of either House, with the permission of the presiding officer

e: A Money Bill can be introduced only by a Minister, in the Lok Sabha, with the recommendation of the President under Articles 109 and 117. A private member cannot introduce it.

q: A Union Territory which has no Legislature of its own:

options.A: Has a separate Consolidated Fund administered by its Lieutenant Governor
options.B: Has a Consolidated Fund kept with the Reserve Bank of India outside the Government accounts
options.C: Has no separate Consolidated Fund of its own, and its receipts and expenditure form part of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: Has a separate fund maintained by the Ministry of Home Affairs outside the accounts of the Union

e: A Union Territory without a Legislature has no separate Consolidated Fund. Its receipts and payments form part of the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 266.

q: When a Proclamation under Article 356 of the Constitution is in operation in a State and the powers of the Legislature of the State are exercisable by Parliament, the Demands for Grants relating to that State are voted by:

options.C: The Legislative Assembly of the State, which continues to sit for financial business

e: When State Legislature powers are exercisable by Parliament during a Proclamation under Article 356, the State Demands for Grants are voted by Parliament.

q: The post-devolution revenue deficit grants recommended by the Fifteenth Finance Commission are payable to those States:

options.A: Whose revenue accounts continue to show a deficit even after taking into account their share in the devolution of central taxes
options.B: All the States, in equal amounts
options.C: Whose revenue accounts show a surplus after devolution
options.D: Which are Special Category States only

e: Post-devolution revenue deficit grants of the Fifteenth Finance Commission go to States whose revenue account still shows a deficit after taking their tax devolution into account.

q: In the Budget documents of the Union Government, the allocations made for the benefit of children under the schemes of the various Ministries are brought together and presented in a separate statement known as the:
e: Ministry-wise allocations benefiting children are consolidated in the Child Budget Statement in the Union Budget documents, separate from the Gender Budget Statement and Outcome Budget.

q: In the departmentalised system of accounts of the Union Government, the Chief Accounting Authority of a Ministry is assisted in the discharge of his budgeting, accounting and internal audit functions by:

options.A: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The Integrated Financial Adviser of the Ministry

e: The Chief Accounting Authority, the Secretary, is assisted by the Integrated Financial Adviser of the Ministry for budgeting, accounting, expenditure control and internal audit functions.

q: The members of the Departmentally Related Standing Committees of Parliament hold office for a term of:
e: Members of the Departmentally Related Standing Committees hold office for a term of one year and are reconstituted annually by the Speaker and the Chairman.

q: Besides the Reserve Bank of India itself, the general banking business of the Government is transacted at a large number of centres through:

options.A: Agency banks appointed by the Reserve Bank of India to conduct Government business on its behalf
options.B: The field offices of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The State cooperative banks, in their own right and not as agents of the Reserve Bank
options.D: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development

e: Government banking business at most centres is done through agency banks appointed by the RBI to conduct Government business on its behalf, besides the RBI itself.

q: A 'follow-up audit' conducted by the organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is primarily intended to:

options.A: Check the accounts of a unit before any payment is made from it
options.B: Assess the action taken by the executive on the findings and recommendations of an earlier audit, and whether the deficiencies noticed in that audit have been remedied
options.C: Check all the transactions of the unit once again, cent per cent
options.D: Examine the Budget Estimates of the audited unit for the ensuing year

e: A follow-up audit assesses action taken by the executive on findings and recommendations of an earlier audit and whether the deficiencies noticed have actually been remedied.

q: Under Section 143(7) of the Companies Act, 2013, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India may, in relation to a Government company, where he considers it necessary:

options.A: Appoint the statutory auditors of the company
options.B: Fix the remuneration payable to the statutory auditors of the company
options.C: Cause a test audit of the accounts of the company to be conducted
options.D: Prepare the annual accounts of the company

e: Under Section 143(7) of the Companies Act, 2013, the CAG may cause a test audit of a Government company where he considers it necessary, in addition to supplementary audit.

q: In the framework for the appraisal and approval of Government schemes, the period for which a scheme is ordinarily approved is aligned with, and the scheme is treated as co-terminus with:

options.A: The period of a Five-Year Plan
options.B: The medium-term framework under the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act
options.C: The annual Budget cycle of the Government
options.D: The award period (cycle) of the Finance Commission

e: In the present appraisal framework, schemes are ordinarily approved co-terminus with the Finance Commission award period or cycle, so that continuation is reviewed with each cycle.

q: Which one of the following is a section of the Public Account of India in the Government system of accounts?

options.C: Loans and Advances by the Central Government

e: Suspense and Miscellaneous is a section of the Public Account of India. Public Debt, Loans and Advances and Capital Outlay belong to the Consolidated Fund sections.

q:
Consider the following statements about the 'net proceeds' of a tax or duty shared between the Union and the States:
1. The net proceeds are ascertained and certified by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, and his certificate in the matter is final.
2. The net proceeds are ascertained and certified by the Finance Commission.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 1 is correct. Under Article 279, net proceeds of a shared tax or duty are ascertained and certified by the CAG and his certificate is final. The Finance Commission does not certify them.

q: The balances of the railway reserve funds are held in the Public Account of India as part of the general cash balances of the Government of India. In respect of these balances:

options.A: No interest is ever credited to the funds
options.B: The balances are invested separately in market securities by the Railway Board
options.C: Interest is credited to the funds by the General Finances at the rate determined for the purpose
options.D: Interest is credited only in the case of the Pension Fund and not of any other fund

e: Railway reserve fund balances form part of general Government cash balances, and interest is credited to the funds by General Finances at the rate determined for the purpose.

q: Besides the Disaster Response Funds, the Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended the creation, at the national level and in the States, of funds devoted to the preparedness for, and mitigation of, disasters, namely the:

options.A: State Disaster Response Funds themselves, with an enlarged corpus

e: Besides Disaster Response Funds, the Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended Disaster Mitigation Funds at the national and State levels for preparedness and mitigation work.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 243J of the Constitution, the Legislature of a State may, by law, make provisions with respect to the maintenance of accounts by the Panchayats and the auditing of such accounts.
2. Under Article 243Z of the Constitution, the Legislature of a State may similarly, by law, make provisions with respect to the maintenance of accounts by the Municipalities and the auditing of such accounts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct. Articles 243J for Panchayats and 243Z for Municipalities empower the State Legislature to make law for maintenance and audit of their accounts.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes AIMS from IPAS on Indian Railways?

options.A: AIMS is the Integrated Payroll and Accounting System, while IPAS is the Accounting Information Management System
options.B: AIMS is the Accounting Information Management System used for the preparation and maintenance of accounts, while IPAS is the Integrated Payroll and Accounting System through which compilation of accounts and payroll are processed
options.C: AIMS is used only for payroll processing, while IPAS is used only for the maintenance of accounts
options.D: There is no difference between the two systems

e: AIMS is the Accounting Information Management System for preparation and maintenance of Railway accounts, while IPAS is the Integrated Payroll and Accounting System for payroll and compilation.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the International Centre for Information Systems and Audit (iCISA) from the International Centre for Environment Audit and Sustainable Development (iCED)?

options.A: iCISA is located at Jaipur and deals with environment audit, while iCED is located at Noida and deals with information systems audit
options.B: iCISA is located at Shimla and deals with environment audit, while iCED is located at Hyderabad and deals with information systems audit
options.C: Both centres are located at Noida and deal with information systems audit
options.D: iCISA is located at Noida and deals with information systems audit, while iCED is located at Jaipur and deals with environment audit

e: iCISA is at Noida and specialises in information systems audit, while iCED is at Jaipur and specialises in environment audit and sustainable development. The locations and subjects are not interchanged.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'e-Lekha' from the Public Financial Management System (PFMS)?

options.A: e-Lekha is the web-based accounting system used for the compilation of the monthly accounts of the Union Government, while PFMS is the platform used for payment, accounting and monitoring of the flow of funds under Government schemes
options.B: e-Lekha is used for monitoring the flow of funds under Government schemes, while PFMS is used for the compilation of the monthly accounts of the Union Government
options.C: e-Lekha is maintained by the Reserve Bank of India, while PFMS is maintained by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Both systems are used only for the preparation of railway salary bills

e: e-Lekha is the web-based system of the Controller General of Accounts for compilation of monthly Union accounts, while PFMS is for payment, accounting and monitoring of funds under Government schemes.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'BharatKosh' from 'e-Kuber'?

options.A: BharatKosh is the core banking solution of the Reserve Bank of India, while e-Kuber is the Non-Tax Receipt Portal of the Government of India
options.B: BharatKosh is the portal for the payment of direct taxes, while e-Kuber is the portal for the sale of Government securities to retail investors
options.C: BharatKosh is the Non-Tax Receipt Portal through which the non-tax receipts of the Government of India are deposited online, while e-Kuber is the core banking solution of the Reserve Bank of India through which Government receipts and payments are processed electronically
options.D: Both are portals maintained by the Controller General of Accounts for the compilation of accounts

e: BharatKosh is the Non-Tax Receipt Portal for online deposit of non-tax receipts of the Government of India, while e-Kuber is the core banking solution of the RBI for Government transactions.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The first Budget of independent India was presented to Parliament in November 1947 by Shri R. K. Shanmukham Chetty.
2. The first Railway Budget of independent India was presented to Parliament in November 1947 by Dr. John Mathai.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct. The first Budget of independent India was presented in November 1947 by R. K. Shanmukham Chetty, and the first Railway Budget by Dr. John Mathai in the same month.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The first Auditor General of India, who assumed charge in the year 1860, was Sir Edmund Drummond.
2. The first Comptroller and Auditor General of independent India was Shri A. K. Chanda.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 1 is correct. Sir Edmund Drummond was the first Auditor General in 1860. The first CAG of independent India was V. Narahari Rao, not A. K. Chanda, who succeeded him.

q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in respect of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department?

options.A: Audit Diwas — 1 April; Motto — 'Seva, Suraksha aur Sahyog'
options.B: Audit Diwas — 16 November; Motto — 'Lokahitarth Satyanishtha' (Dedicated to Truth in Public Interest)
options.C: Audit Diwas — 26 November; Motto — 'Satarkata hi Suraksha hai'
options.D: Audit Diwas — 15 August; Motto — 'Nyaya sabke liye'

e: The Indian Audit and Accounts Department observes Audit Diwas on 16 November, marking the first Auditor General taking charge in 1860, and its motto is Lokahitarth Satyanishtha.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Indian Government Accounting Standard (IGAS) 2 deals with guarantees given by Governments.
2. Indian Government Accounting Standard (IGAS) 3 deals with loans and advances made by Governments — disclosure requirements.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 2 is correct. IGAS 3 deals with loans and advances made by Governments and their disclosure. IGAS 1 deals with guarantees, and IGAS 2 deals with grants-in-aid, so statement 1 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board (GASAB) functions under the aegis of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
2. The accrual-based accounting standards being formulated by GASAB for the Government accounts are known as the Indian Government Financial Reporting Standards (IGFRS).
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct. GASAB functions under the aegis of the CAG, and its accrual-based standards for Government are called Indian Government Financial Reporting Standards, or IGFRS.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Unlike the corresponding authority in the United Kingdom, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India does not exercise the function of controlling the issue of money out of the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India can disallow any item of expenditure and surcharge the officer responsible for it.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 1 is correct. Unlike the UK CAG, the Indian CAG has no comptroller function of controlling issue of money, and he cannot disallow expenditure or surcharge an officer.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A financial (attest) audit provides absolute assurance that no error or fraud exists in the financial statements.
2. The primary responsibility for the prevention and detection of fraud and error in an organisation rests with the management of the organisation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 2 is correct. Financial audit gives only reasonable, not absolute, assurance, and primary responsibility for prevention and detection of fraud and error rests with management.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An Inspection Report issued after local audit is ordinarily divided into Part I, containing serious irregularities requiring the attention of higher authorities, and Part II, containing other, less serious irregularities.
2. Minor irregularities noticed during test audit, which do not call for a detailed Inspection Report, are brought to the notice of the executive through a Test Audit Note.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct. Inspection Reports have Part I for serious irregularities and Part II for others, while minor test audit irregularities are communicated through a Test Audit Note.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The extent of test check exercised by audit in a unit is determined largely by the number of officers posted in the unit.
2. Under the systems-based approach to audit, the emphasis is on cent-per-cent substantive checking of all transactions.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Neither statement is correct. Test check extent depends on internal control, risk and materiality, not staff strength, and systems-based audit relies on controls and samples, not cent-per-cent checking.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An essential feature of a sound system of internal check is that no single person should be allowed to handle a transaction completely from the beginning to the end.
2. Rotation of duties among the staff from time to time is a recognised feature of a sound system of internal control.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct. Sound internal check ensures no one handles a transaction end-to-end alone, and rotation of duties is a recognised internal control feature.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An Internal Audit Charter of an organisation primarily defines the purpose, authority and responsibility of the internal audit function.
2. The scope, coverage and frequency of internal audit of an organisation are fixed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 1 is correct. An Internal Audit Charter defines the purpose, authority and responsibility of internal audit. Its scope and frequency are set by the organisation itself, not by the CAG.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. At the sittings of the Public Accounts Committee, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India presides over the sittings of the Committee.
2. The recommendations made by the Public Accounts Committee in its reports are binding on the Government, which must implement them.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Neither statement is correct. The CAG does not preside over the Public Accounts Committee, he assists it, and PAC recommendations are recommendatory, not binding on Government.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Public Accounts Committee examines the Demands for Grants of the Ministries and votes them before the expenditure is incurred.
2. An Audit Para included in the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is treated as finally settled as soon as the Ministry concerned furnishes its Action Taken Note.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Neither statement is correct. PAC examines accounts and CAG reports after expenditure, it does not vote Demands, and an Audit Para is settled only after PAC examination, not merely on an Action Taken Note.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Minister is eligible to be a member of the Public Accounts Committee, the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings.
2. The Public Accounts Committee and the Estimates Committee are popularly described as 'twin sisters'.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 2 is correct. Ministers are not eligible for membership of PAC, Estimates Committee or Committee on Public Undertakings, and PAC and Estimates Committee are called twin sisters.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Chairperson of the Estimates Committee is appointed by the President of India.
2. One of the functions of the Estimates Committee is to suggest the form in which the estimates shall be presented to Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 2 is correct. The Estimates Committee Chairperson is appointed by the Speaker, not the President, and suggesting the form of presentation of estimates is one of its functions.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Committee on Public Undertakings consists of 22 members — 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.
2. The Committee on Public Undertakings examines the accounts and reports of Indian Railways as a public undertaking.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 1 is correct. COPU has 22 members, 15 from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha. It does not examine Indian Railways, a departmental undertaking examined through other committees.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.
2. Before entering upon his office, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India makes and subscribes an oath or affirmation before the President of India, or some person appointed in that behalf by him.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct under Article 148. The CAG is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal and takes oath before the President before entering office.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The salary of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is equal to the salary of the Chief Justice of India.
2. The conditions of service of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India shall not be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 2 is correct. CAG salary equals that of a Judge of the Supreme Court under the CAG DPC Act, not the Chief Justice, and his service conditions cannot be varied to his disadvantage.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of audit, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is empowered to stop payment of any bill presented to the Accounts office which he considers irregular.
2. The audit of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is confined to the transactions of the Union relating to the Consolidated Fund of India only.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Neither statement is correct. The CAG cannot stop payment of a bill, and his audit covers the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account of the Union and States, not the Consolidated Fund alone.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The statutory auditors of a Government company are appointed by the Board of Directors of the company.
2. For the audit of Government companies, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is assisted by an Audit Board consisting of officers of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department together with outside experts in the relevant fields.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 2 is correct. Statutory auditors of a Government company are appointed by the CAG under the Companies Act, not by the Board, and Audit Boards with outside experts assist in such audits.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Government company is a company in which not less than 51 per cent of the paid-up share capital is held by the Central Government and/or State Governments.
2. Besides the Reports on the Appropriation Accounts and the Finance Accounts of the Union, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India submits to the President a separate Report relating to the accounts of Government companies and public undertakings.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct. A Government company has at least 51 per cent Government paid-up share capital, and the CAG submits a separate report on Government companies and undertakings besides Appropriation and Finance Accounts reports.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The audit of the accounts of a body or authority which is substantially financed by grants or loans from the Consolidated Fund of India is undertaken by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India under the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971.
2. A Utilisation Certificate furnished by a grantee institution serves as evidence for audit that the grant has been repaid to the Government.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 1 is correct. Audit of a substantially financed body is under Section 14 of the CAG DPC Act, 1971. A Utilisation Certificate evidences proper use of the grant, not its repayment.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The audit of receipts conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is limited to verifying the arithmetical accuracy of the cash books of collecting offices.
2. The audit of receipts by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India includes fixing the rates of fares and freight to be charged by the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Neither statement is correct. Receipt audit checks systems for assessment, levy and collection and is not mere arithmetical checking, and fixing Railway fares and freight is an executive function, not audit.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Physical verification of stores and stock is the responsibility of the executive, carried out through the stock-holding officials and stock verifiers.
2. In the audit of stores and stock, the physical verification of stock is carried out by the audit parties of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India themselves.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 1 is correct. Physical verification of stores is an executive responsibility through stock holders and verifiers. Audit examines the system and results and does not itself verify all stock.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Appropriation Accounts, the variation of actual expenditure, shown as excess or savings, is worked out with reference to the original Budget grant only.
2. Explanations for variations between the actual expenditure and the final grant are furnished in the Appropriation Accounts where the variation exceeds the limits prescribed for the purpose.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 2 is correct. Variations in Appropriation Accounts are worked out against the final grant, not the original grant alone, and explanations are given where variation exceeds prescribed limits.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Finance Accounts of the Union Government are presented in two parts — Part I dealing with the Consolidated Fund of India and Part II dealing with the Contingency Fund of India and the Public Account of India.
2. The Finance Accounts of the Union Government include the contractor's ledger of each railway division.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 1 is correct. Finance Accounts Part I covers the Consolidated Fund and Part II covers the Contingency Fund and Public Account. A divisional contractor ledger is not part of Finance Accounts.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The audit which culminates in the certificate of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on the Finance Accounts and the Appropriation Accounts is known as performance audit.
2. Along with the Appropriation Accounts, the Finance Accounts are also laid before Parliament in respect of the accounts of the Union.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The certificate of the CAG on the Finance Accounts and Appropriation Accounts is the outcome of financial or certification audit, not performance audit, so statement 1 is wrong. Under Article 151, the Finance Accounts of the Union are laid before Parliament along with the Appropriation Accounts, so statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In respect of the moneys kept in the Public Account of India, the Government acts in the capacity of a banker or trustee, being liable to repay the moneys to the depositors.
2. Deposits lying in the Public Account of India which remain unclaimed for more than three years are credited to the revenues of the Government as lapsed deposits.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Moneys kept in the Public Account of India under Article 266(2) are held by Government as banker or trustee and must be repaid to the depositors, so statement 1 is correct. Deposits remaining unclaimed for more than three years are credited to Government revenues as lapsed deposits, so statement 2 is also correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Contingency Fund of India is established by Parliament, by law, under Article 267 of the Constitution.
2. Amounts advanced from the Contingency Fund of India are recouped to the Fund automatically at the close of the financial year, without any authorisation by Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Contingency Fund of India is established by Parliament by law under Article 267(1), read with the Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950, so statement 1 is correct. Advances from the Fund are recouped only after Parliament authorises the expenditure through Demands and an Appropriation Act, not automatically, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The unspent balance of a grant remaining at the close of the financial year lapses, and is not available for expenditure in the next year unless voted afresh by Parliament.
2. An order of re-appropriation of funds within a grant, to be valid, must be issued before the expiry of the financial year to which it relates.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: A grant is available only for the year for which it is voted; any unspent balance lapses at the close of the financial year and needs a fresh vote, so statement 1 is correct. An order of re-appropriation is valid only if issued before the expiry of the financial year to which the grant relates, so statement 2 is also correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An excess of expenditure under one grant is condoned merely because there are savings under another grant.
2. Before Excess Grants are voted by Parliament, the excess expenditure reported in the accounts is first examined, and its regularisation recommended, by the Public Accounts Committee.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Excess expenditure under a grant is not condoned merely because savings exist under another grant, since each grant is voted separately, so statement 1 is wrong. Excess expenditure is first examined by the Public Accounts Committee, which recommends its regularisation before Parliament votes Excess Grants under Article 115, so statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 113 of the Constitution, no demand for a grant shall be made except on the recommendation of the President.
2. In respect of the Appropriation Bill, Article 114 of the Constitution provides that no amendment shall be proposed in either House which will have the effect of varying the amount or altering the destination of any grant, or varying the amount of any charged expenditure.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Article 113(2) provides that no demand for a grant shall be made except on the recommendation of the President, so statement 1 is correct. Article 114(2) bars any amendment to the Appropriation Bill that varies the amount or destination of a grant or the amount of charged expenditure, so statement 2 is also correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Expenditure on a new service or new instrument of service not contemplated in the Budget Estimates requires only the sanction of the General Manager of the Railway.
2. The amounts authorised by the Appropriation Act for withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India are specified, service-wise and purpose-wise, in the Finance Bill.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Expenditure on a new service or new instrument of service not contemplated in the Budget requires the prior approval of Parliament, and cannot be sanctioned by the General Manager alone, so statement 1 is wrong. Withdrawals authorised by the Appropriation Act are specified in the Schedule to that Act, not in the Finance Bill, so statement 2 is also wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The classification of transactions in Railway accounts is evolved independently by each zonal Railway to suit its own requirements.
2. The rules and procedure for the compilation, consolidation and presentation of the accounts of Indian Railways are contained in the General Financial Rules.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Classification of transactions follows a uniform system prescribed for all Railways and Government accounts, and is not evolved separately by each zonal Railway, so statement 1 is wrong. Compilation of Railway accounts is governed by the Indian Railway Accounts Code and allied codes, not by the General Financial Rules, so statement 2 is also wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In respect of the accounts of Railways, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India stands relieved of the responsibility of compilation, and the accounts of Railways are compiled by the Railway Accounts Department, while audit remains with the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
2. The internal audit organisation on a zonal Railway functions under the Principal Director of Audit of the Railway.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: For Railways, the CAG has been relieved of compilation; Railway accounts are compiled by the Railway Accounts Department while audit remains with the CAG, so statement 1 is correct. Internal audit on a zonal Railway works under the FA and CAO, not under the Principal Director of Audit, who heads external audit, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the system of associated finance followed on Railways, proposals involving financial implications require the concurrence of the associated finance, that is, the FA&CAO's organisation, before sanction by the competent executive authority.
2. Where the General Manager of a Railway does not accept the financial advice tendered by the FA&CAO, he may overrule the advice without recording any reasons.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Under associated finance, proposals with financial implications need the concurrence of the associated finance, that is the FA and CAO organisation, before the executive sanctions them, so statement 1 is correct. A General Manager who overrules the FA and CAO must record reasons; overruling without recorded reasons is not permitted, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. On a zonal Railway, the FA&CAO functions as the principal financial adviser to the General Manager.
2. The resident audit organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on a zonal Railway is headed by the Principal Director of Audit.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: On a zonal Railway the FA and CAO is the principal financial adviser to the General Manager, so statement 1 is correct. The resident audit organisation of the CAG on a zonal Railway is headed by the Principal Director of Audit, so statement 2 is also correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Depreciation Reserve Fund on Railways is utilised primarily for financing the construction of new lines.
2. Works chargeable to the Development Fund on Railways broadly comprise renewals of track and rolling stock.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Depreciation Reserve Fund finances renewal and replacement of assets, not construction of new lines, which is charged to Capital, so statement 1 is wrong. The Development Fund finances improvement and passenger amenity works, while renewals are met from the DRF, so statement 2 is also wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Block Account in railway commercial accounts shows the distribution of capital-at-charge among the various classes of assets.
2. Under the system of depreciation accounting followed on Railways, an asset whose normal life has expired but which continues in service is written off the Block Account automatically.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Block Account shows how the capital-at-charge of a Railway is distributed among the various classes of assets, so statement 1 is correct. An asset whose life has expired but which is still in service is not automatically written off the Block Account; it stays until it is actually replaced or discarded, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The cost of renewals and replacements financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund forms part of the capital-at-charge of Railways.
2. Before its abolition, the dividend payable by Railways to General Finances was computed on the capital-at-charge excluding the capital invested in strategic lines.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Renewals and replacements financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund do not add to capital-at-charge, which represents capital raised from General Finances, so statement 1 is wrong. Before abolition, dividend was computed on capital-at-charge excluding capital invested in strategic lines, so statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Railway Finance Corporation is registered with the Reserve Bank of India as a scheduled commercial bank.
2. The Indian Railway Finance Corporation finances the acquisition of rolling stock for Railways mainly by budgetary grants from the Ministry of Finance.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation is a non-banking financial company, not a scheduled commercial bank, so statement 1 is wrong. IRFC raises resources mainly through market borrowings and uses them to finance rolling stock acquisition, not through budgetary grants from the Ministry of Finance, so statement 2 is also wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Central audit is conducted at the headquarters office of the audit organisation, to which the vouchers and accounts of the units concerned are sent.
2. Local audit is conducted by the audited office's own staff at its own premises.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: In central audit, vouchers and accounts of field units are sent to the headquarters of the audit organisation where the audit is conducted, so statement 1 is correct. Local audit is conducted by an audit party of the CAG organisation at the premises of the audited office, not by that office's own staff, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Before an audit objection is developed into a Draft Para, the facts stated in the para are got confirmed from the Ministry or department concerned, and its comments are invited.
2. A Provisional Para is a paragraph in the form in which it is proposed to be included in the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, communicated to the Ministry or department for its final comments before the Report is finalised.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Before a Draft Para is finalised, its facts are confirmed from the Ministry or department concerned and its comments are invited, so statement 1 is correct. A Provisional Para is the paragraph in the form proposed for the CAG Report, sent to the Ministry for final comments before the Report is finalised, so statement 2 is also correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the terminology of the Appropriation Accounts, a 'grant' is the amount assigned to meet expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. The amounts authorised by the Appropriation Act for withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India are specified, service-wise and purpose-wise, in the Schedule appended to the Appropriation Act.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: A grant is the amount voted by the Lok Sabha for a service; amounts charged on the Consolidated Fund are covered by an appropriation, not a grant, so statement 1 is wrong. The amounts authorised for withdrawal are specified service-wise and purpose-wise in the Schedule appended to the Appropriation Act, so statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Re-appropriation of funds from the Capital section to the Revenue section of the same grant is permissible with the sanction of the General Manager.
2. Re-appropriation of funds from one grant to another grant is permissible with the approval of the Railway Board.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Re-appropriation between the Capital and Revenue sections of a grant is prohibited, so statement 1 is wrong. Re-appropriation from one grant to another grant is also prohibited, since each grant is a separate authority of Parliament and cannot be changed even by the Railway Board, so statement 2 is also wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Supplementary Demands for Grants of the Government of India are presented to Parliament in batches during the course of the financial year, as and when additional funds are required.
2. The Appropriation Accounts are a Budget document presented to Parliament along with the Annual Financial Statement.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Supplementary Demands for Grants are presented to Parliament in batches during the year as and when additional funds are needed, so statement 1 is correct. Appropriation Accounts are accounts prepared after the year ends and audited by the CAG; they are not a Budget document presented with the Annual Financial Statement, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Vote on Account is generally passed by the Lok Sabha after detailed examination and discussion of the estimates.
2. An exceptional grant forms no part of the current service of any financial year and is made for a special purpose.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: A Vote on Account under Article 116 is passed by the Lok Sabha without detailed discussion of the estimates, to keep services running pending the full Budget, so statement 1 is wrong. An exceptional grant is made for a special purpose and forms no part of the current service of any financial year, so statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The recommendations of the Finance Commission constituted under Article 280 of the Constitution are advisory in character, and not binding on the Government.
2. The Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and four other members.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Recommendations of the Finance Commission under Article 280 are advisory and are not binding on the Government, so statement 1 is correct. Article 280(1) provides that the Finance Commission shall consist of a Chairman and four other members, so statement 2 is also correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The First Finance Commission of India, chaired by Shri K. C. Neogy, was constituted in the year 1951.
2. The Goods and Services Tax Council is chaired by the Prime Minister of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The First Finance Commission, chaired by Shri K. C. Neogy, was constituted in 1951, so statement 1 is correct. The GST Council under Article 279A is chaired by the Union Finance Minister, not by the Prime Minister, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The oath or affirmation made by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India before entering upon his office is in the form set out for the purpose in the First Schedule to the Constitution.
2. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India may resign his office by writing under his hand addressed to the President.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The oath of the CAG is in the form set out in the Third Schedule to the Constitution, not the First Schedule, so statement 1 is wrong. Under Article 148, the CAG may resign his office by writing under his hand addressed to the President, so statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. When a Money Bill is presented to the President for his assent, the President may return the Bill to Parliament for reconsideration.
2. A joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament can be held to resolve a deadlock over a Money Bill.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Under Article 111, the President cannot return a Money Bill for reconsideration; he may only give or withhold assent, so statement 1 is wrong. Article 108 joint sitting does not apply to a Money Bill, on which the Lok Sabha has the final say, so statement 2 is also wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. After the Demands for Grants have been voted by the Lok Sabha, the Appropriation Bill introduced to authorise appropriation from the Consolidated Fund of India is treated as a Money Bill.
2. The Annual Financial Statement, after its presentation, is laid before both Houses of Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Appropriation Bill, introduced after Demands are voted to authorise withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund, is a Money Bill under Article 110, so statement 1 is correct. The Annual Financial Statement is caused to be laid before both Houses of Parliament under Article 112(1), so statement 2 is also correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Annual Financial Statement (Union Budget) is prepared by the Controller General of Accounts.
2. The Economic Survey, which reviews the developments in the economy over the previous year, is prepared by the Reserve Bank of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Annual Financial Statement is prepared by the Ministry of Finance (Budget Division), not by the Controller General of Accounts, so statement 1 is wrong. The Economic Survey is prepared by the Department of Economic Affairs under the Chief Economic Adviser, not by the Reserve Bank of India, so statement 2 is also wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Outcome Budget presented by the Ministries seeks primarily to link the financial outlays provided in the Budget with the measurable outcomes and deliverables expected from them.
2. Performance budgeting, as distinct from traditional line-item budgeting, lays emphasis only on the objects of expenditure, such as salaries and stores.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Outcome Budget links the financial outlays of Ministries with measurable outcomes and deliverables expected from them, so statement 1 is correct. Performance budgeting stresses programmes, activities and results, as against traditional line-item budgeting which stresses only objects of expenditure, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 'Pink Book' of Indian Railways contains principally the Works, Machinery and Plant and Rolling Stock Programmes of the Railways, including the list of sanctioned works.
2. Proforma accounts are prepared in respect of departmental commercial undertakings, such as railway printing presses, so that their commercial results can be ascertained separately.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Pink Book of Indian Railways contains the Works, Machinery and Plant and Rolling Stock Programmes, including the list of sanctioned works, so statement 1 is correct. Proforma accounts are kept for departmental commercial undertakings such as railway printing presses so that their commercial results are known separately, so statement 2 is also correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In order to watch the clearance of the objections raised by Audit in the Inspection Reports, an Objection Book (Register) is maintained by the audit office.
2. The detailed instructions and procedures governing the audit of the accounts of Indian Railways are contained in the Indian Railway Accounts Code.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: the audit office maintains an Objection Book (Register) in which the objections raised in Inspection Reports, particularly those expressible in money value, are entered so that their clearance can be watched. Statement 2 is wrong: the detailed procedure for the audit of Railway accounts is laid down in the CAG's audit manuals and the Regulations on Audit and Accounts, not in the Indian Railway Accounts Code, which governs the executive accounts organisation. Hence 1 only.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The accounts of the Defence Services of the Union are compiled by the Controller General of Accounts.
2. The accounts of Indian Railways are compiled by the Controller General of Accounts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Accounts of the Defence Services are compiled by the Controller General of Defence Accounts, not by the Controller General of Accounts, so statement 1 is wrong. Accounts of Indian Railways are compiled by the Railway Accounts Department, not by the Controller General of Accounts, whose remit is the civil accounts of the Union, so statement 2 is also wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Railway Accounts Department, which compiles the accounts of Indian Railways, is manned principally by officers of the Indian Audit and Accounts Service.
2. The officers who man the audit organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India belong to the Indian Railway Accounts Service.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Railway Accounts Department is manned principally by officers of the Indian Railway Accounts Service, not the Indian Audit and Accounts Service, so statement 1 is wrong. Officers of the CAG audit organisation belong to the Indian Audit and Accounts Service, not the Indian Railway Accounts Service; the two statements interchange the services, so statement 2 is also wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Volume I of the Indian Railway Accounts Code deals principally with traffic accounts and the accounting of earnings and receipts.
2. The Indian Railway Accounts Code, Volume II, deals principally with traffic accounts and the accounting of earnings and receipts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Volume I of the Indian Railway Accounts Code does not deal principally with traffic accounts, so statement 1 is wrong. Volume II of the Code deals principally with traffic accounts and the accounting of earnings and receipts, including the Traffic Book, so statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In audit, the concept of 'materiality' refers to the significance of an omission or misstatement of information, judged by whether it could influence the decisions of the users of the accounts.
2. According to the auditing standards followed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, the audit evidence obtained should be based only on the oral statements of the audited staff.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Materiality in audit means the significance of an omission or misstatement judged by whether it could influence the decisions of users of the accounts, so statement 1 is correct. Audit evidence must be sufficient and appropriate and is gathered from documents and records; it cannot rest only on oral statements of audited staff, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the audit process, an 'entry conference' is held after the audit report is finalised, to communicate the findings to Parliament.
2. In a performance audit, an 'exit conference' is held at the commencement of the audit, to apprise the audited entity of the objectives, scope and criteria of the audit.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: An entry conference is held at the commencement of audit to apprise the audited entity of the objectives, scope and criteria, not after the report is finalised, so statement 1 is wrong. An exit conference is held at the end of audit to discuss findings, not at its commencement; the two definitions are interchanged, so statement 2 is also wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Information Systems (IT) audit conducted by the organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is concerned mainly with examining the controls, security, reliability and integrity of computerised systems through which transactions are processed.
2. An environment audit conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India examines, among other things, the compliance of Government programmes with environmental laws and the performance of the Government in protecting the environment.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: IT audit by the CAG organisation examines controls, security, reliability and integrity of computerised systems through which transactions are processed, so statement 1 is correct. Environment audit examines compliance with environmental laws and Government performance in protecting the environment, so statement 2 is also correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In audit parlance, an auditor is aptly described as a watchdog, and not a bloodhound.
2. Audit can set aside a policy of the Government which it considers wasteful.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The auditor is aptly described as a watchdog and not a bloodhound, watching on behalf of the taxpayer without assuming dishonesty, so statement 1 is correct. Audit cannot set aside or replace a Government policy; it can only report on economy, efficiency and effectiveness of its implementation, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Internal audit by the Railway Accounts Department reports to the management of the Railway itself.
2. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is an independent constitutional authority and is not an officer of Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Internal audit by the Railway Accounts Department is an aid to Railway management and reports to that management itself, so statement 1 is correct. The CAG is an independent constitutional authority under Articles 148 to 151 and is not an officer of Parliament, so statement 2 is also correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Performance audit conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is also popularly described as certification audit.
2. Under the framework of the International Standards of Supreme Audit Institutions (ISSAI), public-sector auditing comprises three broad types, namely financial audit, performance audit and compliance audit.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Certification audit is the audit of financial statements leading to the CAG certificate; performance audit, which examines economy, efficiency and effectiveness, is a different audit, so statement 1 is wrong. Under the ISSAI framework, public sector auditing comprises financial audit, performance audit and compliance audit, so statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the case of a Government company, the statutory auditors are appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India under Section 139(5) of the Companies Act, 2013.
2. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India may conduct a supplementary audit of the accounts of a Government company within 120 days from the date of receipt of the audit report of the statutory auditors.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: For a Government company, statutory auditors are appointed by the CAG under Section 139(5) of the Companies Act, 2013, so statement 1 is correct. Under Section 143(6), the CAG may conduct a supplementary audit within 60 days of receipt of the statutory auditors report, not 120 days, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An Audit Para included in the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is treated as finally settled when the Public Accounts Committee accepts the action taken by the Government on the para.
2. The reports of the Public Accounts Committee are generally unanimous and no minutes of dissent are appended to them.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: An Audit Para is treated as finally settled when the Public Accounts Committee accepts the action taken by Government on it, so statement 1 is correct. By convention, reports of the Public Accounts Committee are generally unanimous and no minutes of dissent are appended to them, so statement 2 is also correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The control exercised by the Public Accounts Committee over public expenditure is essentially post-expenditure (post-mortem) control, exercised after the moneys have been spent, on the basis of the accounts and the Audit Reports.
2. Besides the Appropriation Accounts of the Union Government and the Reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India thereon, the Public Accounts Committee also examines the estimates of the Ministries before they are voted.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Public Accounts Committee exercises post-expenditure control, examining accounts and CAG Reports after money has been spent, so statement 1 is correct. Examining estimates before they are voted is the function of the Estimates Committee, not of the PAC, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Minister is eligible to be a member of any of the three Financial Committees of Parliament.
2. The members of the Committee on Public Undertakings hold office for a term of one year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: A Minister is not eligible to be a member of the Public Accounts Committee, the Estimates Committee or the Committee on Public Undertakings, so statement 1 is wrong. Members of the Committee on Public Undertakings hold office for a term of one year, so statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Chairperson of the Committee on Public Undertakings is elected by the members of the Committee from amongst themselves.
2. The Committee on Public Undertakings examines the Appropriation Accounts of Indian Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Chairperson of the Committee on Public Undertakings is appointed by the Speaker from amongst its Lok Sabha members, not elected by the Committee, so statement 1 is wrong. Examination of the Appropriation Accounts of Railways is the work of the Public Accounts Committee, not of the Committee on Public Undertakings, so statement 2 is also wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways does not ordinarily consider matters of day-to-day administration of the Ministry of Railways.
2. The members of the Departmentally Related Standing Committees of Parliament are nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha from amongst the members of their respective Houses.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Departmentally Related Standing Committees do not ordinarily consider matters of day-to-day administration of the Ministry concerned, so statement 1 is correct for the Committee on Railways. Members of these Committees are nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha from their respective Houses, so statement 2 is also correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Large and persistent savings under a grant, noticed year after year, are regarded in audit as indicative of efficient financial management by the executive.
2. Savings anticipated in a grant during the course of a financial year should be surrendered as soon as they are foreseen, without waiting for the close of the year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Large and persistent savings year after year indicate defective budgeting and poor estimation, not efficient financial management, so statement 1 is wrong. Under the General Financial Rules, savings anticipated in a grant should be surrendered as soon as foreseen, without waiting for the close of the year, so statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where expenditure under a sub-head of a grant exceeds the provision under that sub-head, but the excess is offset by savings under other sub-heads and the total amount of the grant is not exceeded, no Excess Grant is required.
2. Interest paid on capital borrowed for the execution of a work, during the period of construction of that work, is ordinarily charged to the revenue (working expenses) of the year in which it is paid.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: If total expenditure stays within the grant, excess under one sub-head met by savings under others needs only re-appropriation and no Excess Grant, so statement 1 is correct. Interest on capital during construction is charged to Capital as part of the cost of the work, not to revenue working expenses, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where an error in the classification of a transaction is noticed after the accounts of the month have been closed, it is rectified by a transfer entry in the accounts of a subsequent month, the closed accounts not being reopened.
2. The cash balance held by the Government of India is accounted for as part of the Public Account of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: A classification error found after monthly accounts are closed is corrected by a transfer entry in a subsequent month; closed accounts are not reopened, so statement 1 is correct. In the Finance Accounts, the net cash balance of Government is included under the Public Account, which has Cash Balance as one of its sectors, so statement 2 is also correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 283 of the Constitution, the custody of the Consolidated Fund of India and the Contingency Fund of India, and the payment of moneys into and the withdrawal of moneys from them, are regulated by law made by Parliament or, until such law is made, rules made by the President.
2. Under Article 284 of the Constitution, all moneys received by, or deposited in the custody of, an officer of the Union or a court in connection with the affairs of the Union, other than revenues or public moneys credited to the Consolidated Fund, shall be paid into the Contingency Fund of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Article 283 provides that custody of the Consolidated Fund and Contingency Fund and payments into and withdrawals from them are regulated by law of Parliament or, until then, rules made by the President, so statement 1 is correct. Under Article 284 such moneys are paid into the Public Account of India, not the Contingency Fund, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Appropriation Accounts of a grant include the Profit and Loss Account of the Railway undertaking.
2. A statement showing the position of the public debt of the Government of India forms part of the Finance Accounts of the Union Government.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Appropriation Accounts only compare grant or appropriation with actual expenditure for each service; they do not include any Profit and Loss Account, so statement 1 is wrong. A statement of the public debt of the Government of India forms part of the Finance Accounts of the Union Government, so statement 2 is correct.
